The product's farewell as the homepage: the app icon, 'A farewell to Arc', a dated sunset, then a long letter signed by hand. Ending a product with a letter instead of a banner.
A plain statement of what the research teams study, topic tabs with paper counts, then each paper paired with an artwork (a black hole in marbled blue and gold). Research made browsable by art.

A purple illustrated scene of a robot debugging on a stage, then sections separated by hand-drawn pink squiggles ('New issue at 2am. PR is ready for review.'). A dev tool with a cartoon world and a sense of humour.
The page is a fake desktop OS: windows, a dock, and the hedgehog mascot illustrated on the product window. The brand's whole site behaves like an operating system.
A desk and chair placed on a mountain meadow at dusk fill the hero, the headline small and centred above. Mercury's signature: the office moved into a landscape, then the real product on dark.
Big flat brand shapes in orange, black and green frame the editor full of real social templates, then a magenta section with finished assets. The product's output fills the page.
A prompt box over a grid of generated 3D objects (axolotl, chameleon, guitar, samurai helmet) on black. A 3D generator proven by a shelf of what it made.
A plain small title then a loose grid of editorial images: an illustrated cover, a book with a red ribbon, a woman with an egg-shaped lamp. Community editorial with almost no chrome.
A large serif paragraph of who he is beside a round portrait, then sections separated by rules (About me, Type design) with his own typefaces. A personal site that reads like a book page.
A deep red field with a hand-drawn logo, a serif 'Hi, I'm Ethan' with linked words, then his journal and book covers as poster tiles ('YOU DESERVE A TECH UNION'). Warm, political, typographic.
Her name broken into letters scattered over a grid, red translucent blocks and a greyscale photo overlapping: a CSS layout expert whose homepage is a layout experiment.

A big serif masthead and ruled header like a newspaper, then a yellow hero where every line of the headline sits on its own white highlight strip, and courses as poster tiles. An independent publisher with a strong print voice.
A soft blob hero ringed with contributor avatars, then article cards with pastel gradient edges and tall condensed headlines. A tech publication with a crafted, human look.
Each day of links is introduced by a full orange block with the date set huge in outlined numerals ('11/24 Tuesday'). A daily link list given rhythm by its own calendar.
A huge green and black eye graphic fills the lead story, then a grid where type specimens ('Ciao') sit next to photos. A design magazine whose covers are typographic.

A full-width photo of a soft textile creature with a lowercase headline over it, then a bright yellow band with an illustrated 'states of motion' chapter. Architecture and design news with art-directed chapters.
'Nara Slab' stacked five times in shrinking sizes as the hero, then colour tiles for each category (variable fonts, superfamilies, global scripts). The specimen is the hero.
The font list is the homepage: each family's name set in itself (Esperanza, Cosmica Mono, Obbligato...) as a stack of ruled lines, next to one big gradient letter. An index that is also the specimen.
'Antique Mono Legacy' in big red letters, then a black band of letters sliding and overlapping ('mica', 'itmica'), then colour blocks per family. A Swiss foundry with movement.
A lime green page with a monospace intro crossed by a hand-drawn scribble, then 'Little Flying Elephant' in a huge heavy sample with live tester controls. Playful and loud.
Each family is a grey card where its name is set as a poem of glyphs, arrows, brackets and numbers ('Atelier ↳ Giotti / Ⅲ “World” Heritage / [Ionic] 4M'). The character set shown off as copy.
One huge cropped 'C' on an orange field and a small grid of 'Ag' samples. An open-source foundry with a single typographic move.
A huge, soft, blobby wordmark across the top, then the catalogue as four big rows with counts (Sans serif 66, Serif 27, Monospace 23, Display 47). Navigation as the page.

'JetBrains Mono. A typeface for developers_' set in the font with a blinking cursor, then giant 'An' and 'Src:' specimens annotated with what each design choice fixes. A specimen that explains its decisions.
The word 'recursive' set in a grid where every letter shifts weight and slant, then a page laid out like code comments with live sliders for each variable axis. The font's axes are the interaction.
A flat illustration of a synth keyboard, a watch and paper clips made of the icon style, then a live toolbar (weight, size, colour) over the icon grid. The product's style becomes the scene.
One line of headline, then the search field and the full icon grid sit right in the first screen. A catalogue lets the inventory be the hero instead of describing it.
Today's pick shown big inside a browser window, with its date and a one-line review under it, then an archive feed of smaller picks. A gallery's hero is the latest thing it chose.
The illustrated people run, leap and stride around a huge serif wordmark, so the hero is a sample of the product. An illustration kit shows its figures in action, never a static grid.
Black chrome, small type and filter pills, then a three-column grid of colourful site thumbnails. A gallery stays dark and quiet so the work it collects carries all the colour.

site: A Journal on How to Wow People
note: A black page with the printed issue photographed mid-flip, then one centred serif paragraph that says what the magazine is. A print publication sells the object and its voice, nothing else.
The hero is a hex dump in grey mono with the line 'Technology real estate runs on.' set beside it, as quiet as the data. An engineering page for a proptech shows the raw bytes instead of a dashboard.
An EV charging under a carport in a forest, with tiny live labels (charging, 11.2 kW) pinned on the photo. Energy software shown as the real home it controls, the UI reduced to two annotations.
Heavy condensed caps headline, then four product tiles in saturated colours, each with one 3D furniture object. A B2B catalogue tool borrows the playful colour of a toy shop for its feature cards.
A purple duotone photograph of a model cityscape fills the screen with mono essay credits overlaid like a terminal. A think tank's journal looks like an archive document, not a website.
Each event is a full-bleed photo of the room with its title centred large over it, stacked down the page. A venue's homepage is its programme, every night given a whole screen.
A serif headline with a hand-drawn underline, then a huge orange ribbon looping around a paper envelope. One oversized illustrated object carries the whole brand of a reading tool.

A serif headline over dark sea water with a mono stats row, then the red ASIC board photographed on white with red highlighted words in the text. Deep tech pairs nature texture with the real board, and one red carries both.
The specimen is written as an 'Official Travel Guide' to Montreal, with postcards, city photos and mixed-colour italic display lines. A typeface sold through a story about the city it is named after.

The heat pump stands lit in a black void like a monolith, headline and CO2 numbers small beside it, then a second shot of the unit in a raking light. Industrial hardware photographed with the drama of a luxury object.

Text spirals into a vortex beside the headline, and '~00 hours lost per project' is set as a giant numeral. A dev starter kit made to look like a design publication, with the cost of not using it as the biggest number.

A baker loading bread in the oven fills the hero, then a full electric-blue block with caps and handwritten words mixed in the same line. A local shop with the energy of a zine: one loud colour and a hand-drawn voice.

The headline 'Where science meets software.' is split across the hero, its last word pushed to the far corner, with a mint moiré circle between. A health company shows precision through a generative pattern, not stock lab photos.
A chrome, glowing 3D wordmark mixing Latin and kanji fills the hero, then a manifesto in caps over the chrome tubes. A collectibles brand makes its logo the main 3D object.
The hero is a field of scattered numbers in small colour tags at random sizes, the largest '100' sitting at the bottom. A studio shows a number cloud instead of a showreel, data as decoration.
A sunflower-yellow block holds the headline and two buttons next to the Sunflowers painting itself. A museum takes its UI colour from its most famous work.
Giant 'Aspen' and 'Search' and 'PLACING WINNERS.' blocks alternate with grey halftone textures and one mint panel. A recruiting firm for quants looks like a Swiss poster grid, not a staffing agency.
Album covers and objects fly in an arc over a faint handwritten script, then a serif italic 'Storytelling'. A musician's site arranges artefacts like a mood board in motion.

Soft white 3D renders with iridescent highlights and a large statement 'For decades, people learned the language of machines. Now machines learn ours.' A designer's site is a calm exhibition of renders.
First and last name set huge at the two edges of the screen over a black-and-white portrait, then a dark grid of brand work. A personal site where the name is the layout.
A digital artwork shown on a screen inside a dark room, then a 'You're viewing' strip of works with small thumbnails. Digital art presented in situ, as an object in a space.

Plain text on brown with a live 'grid-aware mode' notice and a carbon counter in the header; even the 404 section is 'Emissions not found'. A research project about web emissions designs with the fewest bytes and shows it.
'It's week 48. Six days of this week are still open.' is computed from today, under a phone showing the habit grid. App copy that knows the date makes a generic phone hero feel alive.

'Find your financial independence date.' in a serif with the key words in italic, then three numbered steps and a live calculator that returns a date. A finance tool promises one concrete output and lets you compute it on the page.
Four large studio portraits of the doctors fill the page, with the practice's address and hours in tiny type at the top. A medical practice sells trust through faces at full size, not stock icons.
A soft pastel gradient, 'forever' in serif italic, and the hero CTA is a field prefilled 'portrait.so/robert' to claim your name. A personal-page product puts the URL you will own in the hero.
A sunset photo of a wooden lamp, then each product shown as a thin wireframe drawing with one coloured part. A DIY furniture brand shows its pieces as assembly drawings, the way you will build them.
A heavy yellow 'CASSETTE' spans the top, then equalizer bars made of yellow strips and a cut-paper collage of a cassette. A music agency turns its name and a sound meter into the whole identity.
Mono caps title and each story with its own vivid commissioned illustration in a rounded tile on black. An online magazine whose grid is a wall of art, one style per writer.
One screen: a skull logo, the name and the address in caps inside stacked outlined frames, like a card on a pile. A secretive company says only who and where.
A peach page of small type listing past roles, products and press, with a now-playing track and a pixel grid of 'clanker commits'. A designer's CV made personal by two live details.
A dense grid of record-cover-like artworks, each a track of a playlist with a mini player. A music project lets the covers be the page.

A painterly gradient of orange, blue and green with a centred serif 'Humanist Superintelligence', and the same paintings on every news card. An AI lab takes a warm, brushed palette instead of the usual dark neon.
A black-and-white photo of rolling golf links with a tiny figure, headline at the bottom left, then beige panels. A golf investment firm sells the landscape, not the sport.
A toy-like boxer figure stands behind the typeface name in yellow, the weights listed on both sides, then '1825' set huge. A display face sold with a mascot that shares its character.

The studio name in heavy condensed caps spans the whole width, then a pink product shot and one caps claim 'No agency has put more new brands on Australian retail shelves.' A packaging studio shows one bold claim and the packs.
A giant 'a' drawn with its bezier points visible, numbered 'design, system, platform', on red then green panels of styles. A type system sold by showing how its letters are built.
Acoustic booths photographed in warm raking light, a butterfly on stone for calm, and tiny type in large white margins. An office product sold through mood and light, like furniture.
'CONSIDERED CUPS' in thin caps over a close-up pour, then an olive block with the story in thin caps and shop photos. A coffee chain builds its brand from one thin typeface and one olive.
A heavy black headline over an orange halftone image of oil pumps and machinery. Enterprise software for rental and service companies shows their industrial world, printed like a poster.
A huge red serif wordmark across the top, then a satellite map of every shop and restaurant that sells the oil, listed beside it. A small producer proves its reach with a map, not testimonials.
'Learn how to design fonts like a pro' in red condensed caps over a giant red serif 'aa' pair. A type foundry sells its book with the letters themselves as the hero image.
The studio's name set huge in a grey serif, split across the width, then a vivid conference poster at full size. A studio introduced by its name and one loud piece of work.
The MICR banking typeface's digits as the specimen, and the checkout (licence choice, price, pay button) sits right in the first screen. A one-product foundry where buying is the landing page.
A red serif sentence with black clauses, then a warm sauna portrait at full height with mono deliverables lists. A growth agency shows one client's world in a single photograph.
The product's laptop sits on a stack of books, binders and a coffee cup under a centred headline. Enterprise AI shown on the pile of work it replaces.
The fund's name in heavy caps across the top, then a pastel sunburst behind a mono caps sentence 'We're building the seed fund we wish we had.' A VC that reads like a record sleeve.

The prompt is a sentence whose words are coloured editable chips ('A driving trap track with percussion, synth bass and flute, 140 BPM, 1:00') beside a playing orb. A generator's hero teaches you the prompt grammar by example.
Die-cast cars tumble across saturated orange, green and purple blocks, each block one claim with the app screen. A collector app makes the collected objects the hero, at toy scale.
The wordmark's letters hold an architecture photo, then essays with serif titles beside large black-and-white space photographs. A design publication whose logo is a frame for images.
A serif statement with London and Los Angeles underlined, under a huge serif 'H+H' glyph drawn like a ligature. An agency's logo set big enough to be the hero image.
'BOLD FLAVOR' in orange condensed caps spans the width over brown, the jar of sauce below. A food brand whose headline literally is the product promise, set like a spice label.
A grey page of mono text, one orange desert photograph and a list of papers with dates. An AI research lab presents itself as a working document.
A dense grid of material swatches (stone, pigment, wood, textile) under a search bar and category filters. A materials archive where every tile is a sample.
The homepage is a table of years, clients, disciplines and studios, a hundred rows long. A designer's whole career as one plain index.
'Say hello to Memo' over a photograph of the home robot handling a wine glass in a real kitchen. A robot shown doing a delicate chore, not posing.
Red, teal and blue blocks tile the page, each holding an exhibition photo, its dates and a short title. An art centre whose layout is itself a coloured composition.
Candy bar wrappers in every flavour colour fill the hero, tilted and overlapping, with the studio's one-line pitch over them. A brand studio leads with a pile of the packaging it made.
A hand holds the phone with the check-in card, and a row of real customers stands in a queue along the bottom of the page. A loyalty tool shows the line of people it serves.
Barcode-like vertical bars mark three numbered themes, then the name runs off the page in giant black type on white. An AI data company uses a data texture instead of a neural glow.
The typeface name surrounded by comic 'BANG' and 'KABOOM' bursts and sticker labels, then weight lists on purple and yellow panels. A cartoonish face sold in its own comic-book world.

Each release is a full-width row with a chunky outlined 'RELEASE' label and the title in huge type, alternating red and green, under an op-art header. A record label's homepage is its discography, set like a festival poster.
'The TypeScript MCP framework' set in blackletter, beside a live metrics panel of tool calls. A developer framework uses one unexpected typeface to stand out from every other docs-style homepage.
A photo of the cooks at work, then the whole pitch in large green text with the opening hours set beside it at the same weight. A butcher-burger spot treats its hours as headline information.
A blurred black-and-white street photo, then tiny type columns with lyrics, credits and show dates beside small band photos. A band site that reads like a liner note.
Heavy condensed caps stacked on two greens, the call to action a tilted white sticker 'BECOME A MEMBER'. A social club's site written as a protest poster.

The name in giant caps across the top, one serif sentence with an italic clause, then photos of the room keys, menus and perfumes it designed. A hotel branding studio shows the objects a guest touches.
A blurred macro photo of plants under the giant name, then the featured face 'Avec' as a large specimen with a Moholy-Nagy quote set in it. A foundry whose homepage is a rotating feature.
A plain table of songs, artists, the people who submitted them, their city and a feeling, in blue mono with play buttons. A time capsule made of one list, the data is the design.
One long sentence introduces the organist, each role set in a different blue or grey, then a video and a dated events list. A musician's bio as a single typographic sentence.
A vertical rule divides the page and the name and roles stack against it at different sizes, with the brand name ghosted huge in grey behind. A personal site that is one typographic composition.
A heavy black wordmark with stair-stepped letters fills a hot-pink hero, then a calm cream section with the founder's portrait. A studio puts all its noise in the logo and stays quiet after.
A pink hero cut by a white cloud shape holds the exhibition title and dates, then the artists listed in a centred column beside the works. A gallery whose layout echoes the show's mood.

A cut-out object (a jar with a paintbrush) on purple, a yellow notice bar, then the month's events as a dated calendar of photo cards. A contemporary art museum leads with its programme, in its own odd colours.
Product screens, photos and little illustrated characters are cut out and pasted around the headline. A design studio shows its range as a playful collage instead of a case-study grid.
Faces, ingredient macros, product tubes and line diagrams are pinned together like a research scrapbook. A sunscreen brand shows its science and its users on the same wall.
Sculptural stone gratings photographed as objects on beige plinths, with a large 'Made to matter' at the bottom. An industrial product shot as if it were gallery sculpture.
The CV is a list of past companies written as huge domain names (monograph.com, figma.com), over a faint wall of SQL. A designer-engineer lets the URLs he built be the headline.
The name 'OMA APPEL' is set in red and mirrored upside down below itself, as is every section heading. A small jam maker gets a whole identity from one typographic trick.
The whole page is framed by green football-pitch markings, with the sales product UI on the field. A sales tool commits to one metaphor and draws it as the layout.
A full-width gallery photo of the current show, then exhibitions as large titles with dates and installation photos. A museum that lets the rooms and the works do all the talking.
A blue network map of labelled nodes fills the hero, then a plain table of projects with client and discipline. A data-design studio leads with a visualization and lists its work as data.
A black-and-white sculpture on a plinth, then a full-width red macro texture and a cloth-bound dictionary in raking light. A studio shows its taste through materials, not case studies.

site: Eleven Plants for Dum-Dums & Cool Ppl
note: A green poster with a numbered list of eleven plants and their Latin names between two botanical drawings in ovals, then each plant on its own cream page. A list article designed as a printed poster series.
The name in huge black type with a vivid 3D object sitting inside the O, then a black index of capabilities and clients. One rendered object turns a plain wordmark into the hero.
A dotted display face fills the hero, then each typeface is a tile with its own sample sentence in olive, slate and black. A foundry catalogue where every tile writes copy for its face.
A wavy, warped serif headline floats over a soft photo of a person, then a lavender section of phones in hands. A journaling app makes its headline look like a dream.
A black hero fading into fine horizontal lines, then a full coral block with the mission in large light type. Robotics presented with two colours and one texture, no robot.
A small intro line, then a staircase of square tiles, each a project (a self-driving car, a balloon, a robot arm) on its own colour. A lab shows its range as a growing grid, not a list.
Each typeface is one ruled row with a sample sentence in its own voice, Japanese and German mixed in ('At Casa di Solare, フォント forever'). A foundry index where the copy shows what each face is for.
The name in a huge serif over an overhead photo of people working, then plain stats on cream (.2 Billion, 10,000+, SEC, 2017). A wealth manager for tech workers shows the office and four facts.
The hero is a mountain drawn in ASCII characters across the whole width, then fashion photos with small mono product labels. A design-and-tech agency signs its craft with code-made imagery.

Green glassy 3D letters spell the name, then a note that the festival is on hiatus and a dense list of every past artist. An event page in its archive state: thanks, photos and the full line-up as a record.
The name in a huge heavy serif across the top, then a row of the packaging it designed and a centred serif paragraph with a small flower drawing. A branding studio as a printed catalogue.

A blurred TV colour-bar glow behind an iPad showing a camera feed, a serif headline with one italic word, and an App Store button stuck on like a yellow price sticker. A utility app with the warmth of an old TV ad.

A dark page with world clocks for its studios, then an aerial photo of Manhattan captioned 'Empire State Building, Immersive Sonic Experience'. A sound studio shows places, because sound has no picture.

A large serif headline above a band of black and purple vertical stripes like a barcode or document stack, then a search field across purple stripes. Legal AI shown as a texture of documents, not a robot.
The fund is a single pale card with the name in a large serif, and the portfolio arrives as more cards stacked beneath it. A small fund presents itself like letters on a desk.

The name in huge white type, then each card game as a tile with a soft 3D suit icon, and a 'What should we make next?' grid with vote counts. A games studio lets players vote on the roadmap from the homepage.

A player sitting on a bench against a red clay court wall, a serif paragraph about the state of the sport, then the products on white. A tennis brand shot like a magazine story, products after the mood.
A painted valley and cliffs fill the product section, with a faint ASCII trace beside a small headline. An agent-monitoring tool takes the calm of a landscape painting instead of a dashboard.
A full orange block with 'GOOD Meat at the butchery.' next to a photo of a shopper at the meat counter. Lab-grown meat sold as already normal, in a real shop.

A heavy retro script wordmark sits above a dandelion field photo with the bottle in it and the question 'Do you like butter?'. A perfume named for a scent leads with the scent's image and a playful question.
Hands cutting tomatoes, then each knife laid on its own saturated background (red, blue). A craft brand pairs process photos with flat colour product shots.
A full-width photo of golden light on water, the new album announced in yellow mono caps, then the film and a yellow sign-up block. A musician's release page in two colours taken from the cover.
Four photos of people working from home hang on hand-drawn strings over a tan panel, beside a plain-spoken manifesto. A VC fund shows the life it invests in, scrapbook style.
Macro photos of a terrazzo-like surface alternate with a hand-drawn scientist at his flasks. A material made from waste is shown both as texture and as the lab story behind it.
Under 'Your attention is sacred', a wall of dozens of small photos of members holding their phones away. A focus product shows its community as the proof.
'IT'S AN OPINION IN YOUR MOUTH' in tall condensed caps next to a cut-out burger, then the chef's name split huge in a serif. A burger chain designed like a fashion magazine.
The name in huge thin type over a photo of workers in orange workwear, then a grid of customer portraits under 'Perspectives from the frontline of AI'. Applied AI shown through people in the field.
An orange page with chunky display headings, a featured story of a flower-market cat, then rounded panels of stories and animal profiles. A pet magazine with the warmth of a children's book.
A huge close-up of open lips with the name 'Op e n' spaced across the mouth, then a black-and-white portrait. A mindfulness studio shows breath, not calm stock imagery.
Bags photographed in use, in studios and on boats, packed into an irregular grid with bold black captions. A modular bag brand presented like a zine spread.
'Tell sales emails to just stop', then a full red panel with an open letter 'Dear Salespeople, ...' signed 'Everyone'. An email blocker's pitch written as a letter to the people it blocks.
Landscape photos each with the three colours extracted below them, filterable by Desert, Ocean, Rock. A palette tool whose homepage is the tool's output.
A huge yellow hand-drawn wordmark over a glossy liquid surface with tiny figures sliding on it. A personal-care product made playful through scale.
A soft profile portrait fading into white with 'Beyond Humanware' in small type and three pill tags. A wearable AI device sold through the person, not the hardware.
A long sentence where the first clause is black and the rest fades to grey, then two phones each showing one gradient sun. A breathing app whose copy breathes out.

Vertical stripes of named colours (burnt orange, soft butter, uranus) run down the right of the hero, then the whole palette as a list of coloured rows. A colour tool whose layout is the colour list itself.
An exploded render of a device (case, board, buttons) under a heavy headline, then a blue gradient section with the product. Software for hardware teams leads with the hardware.
A mechanical keyboard photographed in black with one red key, the name 'Altar II' in a serif, and a red Kickstarter strip. A small hardware maker shoots its object like a luxury watch.
A white chip render on white, the headline's second sentence fading to grey. A CPU startup made calm and architectural, no neon.
Found colour photographs (blue doors, yellow walls) scattered on grey around an outlined title. A photo essay laid out like pinned prints.
One screen: an isometric office in line drawing with a few coloured objects and a colleague counter. A one-joke site that is the whole experience in a single view.
A flat pink illustration of a chair and window behind 'Say hello to materium!', then soft-lit furniture photos on white. A furniture brand starts with a drawing before the product.
The page reads like a paper: dense justified text, a small world map drawing and a multilingual index in the corner. A protocol presented as a thesis, not a token.
Thin grid lines frame a spec table, one red dot as the record button, then each film made with the app as a 'Study' with its filmmaker. A camera app whose showcase is a numbered series of films.
White robot arms reaching in the dark under a serif headline, then a chrome globe labelled 'World Model'. An AI lab mixes documentary hardware with one symbolic object.
A red engraved robin on near-black beside a spaced serif wordmark, the about text in two serif columns. A one-person fund with the look of a private bookplate.
Glowing 3D icon tiles across the top, then each day's launch on a vertical timeline with its own icon. A launch week page that stays as the record once the week is over.

'GROW NEW' in heavy green condensed caps over dark green, then an aerial photo of terraced crops beside a pale green panel 'A new way to protect the planet'. Crop science shown from above, as landscape.
'(GOOGLE VENTURES) EST. 2009' set like a newspaper masthead in tall condensed type, then portfolio stories as magazine covers. A VC firm whose homepage reads like a publication.

An elephant mascot in a spacesuit next to a rocket in a purple space illustration, then the app on every device. A social client sold through character and craft, the same way its maker did for Tweetbot.
'inspiration is everywhere. and nowhere.' in heavy type above a 3D sculpture of moss-covered rock with one butterfly. An ideas app represented by a single strange object.

'Don't type, just speak.' in a large serif with italics, a line of transcribed text trailing across the page into a waveform, then a dark green panel comparing 45 wpm with 220 wpm. Voice input shown as words flowing out.
A dark green hero holds a collage of fabric swatches, glass and iridescent material shots, then the collectible objects on beige. An interior studio leads with its materials before its rooms.
The name built from heavy black arches and half-circles sits above a strip of interior photos, then a serif statement. Geometric shapes turned into a wordmark that echoes architecture.
A timber house under eucalyptus fills the hero, then an orange 'Architecture, Built for Life.' and a three-photo project row. Builders who let the finished houses do the talking.
'Down the long driveway, you'll see it' set huge in white on black above one photo of a mid-century house. A photo book's site written as an invitation.
'History-making profits. World-ending emissions.' with each oil major's profit scattered across black in red, then a full orange download bar. A data campaign where the numbers are the layout.
A hand reaching for a small lamp in soft light, then a long serif sentence about light as architecture. A lighting studio sells mood through one gesture.
A dense grid of designed objects (a vase, a stool, a blue pill, a horse sculpture), each with a tiny label. A curation site that is all inventory and no chrome.
A huge black serif 'HOUSE of HONEY' over pink, a maximal interior photo, then a burgundy panel with a pink script. An interiors studio as loud and layered as its rooms.
'Czechia's first Medicine 3.0 clinic' with the last words in grey, then a long grey serif philosophy. A clinic that reads like a journal, not a hospital.
A large crop of a concrete ceiling, then the nav itself set large (ABOUT, WORK, REPOSITORY) beside a list of buildings with places. An architecture office whose menu is the page's typography.
The book with a round green sticker, a centred description, then cut-out tree silhouettes standing along the bottom. A book about tree drawings shows the trees as the decoration.
Cut-out figures, fried eggs and a sword float around a serif masthead, then the programme as a dated table with ticket buttons. A theatre poster that turns into a box office.
Dozens of small note cards scattered across the page, then a serif essay with references. An essay site whose hero is the notes it came from.
A plain table of films with year, director, country and genre in red type. A film list as a single sortable table, nothing else.

A giant lime pixel-art chevron sits behind 'NEXT-GEN PYTHON TOOLING', then olive panels with live benchmark bars (0.16s vs 3.25s). A Python toolchain with the attitude of a game, its speed shown as a race.
A smiling pink star mascot beside 'Gleam is a friendly language', a full pink band for sponsors, then code on dark. A programming language that leads with warmth instead of benchmarks.
Each section is a full-width colour band (teal 'Why Rust?', purple 'Build it in Rust', red 'Get involved'). A language homepage where colour alone separates the chapters.
A black banner with the logo, then the homepage is a plain document: intro, motivation, quick start, a book cover. A library whose plainness is its argument.
'POINT OF VIEW' in giant red condensed caps around a circled logo, then a stage photo over walls of text. A conference that looks like a gig poster.
A woman standing in a canoe at sunset fills the hero, then exhibition installation shots and a row of issue covers. A photography magazine whose site is a gallery wall.
'Base OFF MUTE' set huge with custom glyphs, then the podcast as a ruled list of episodes with dot-matrix subtitles and durations. A podcast homepage that is its episode list.
Large soft close-ups of skin and lips, then a serif paragraph about a personalised approach. An aesthetic clinic photographed like a beauty campaign.
The three words of the name on tilted coloured cards (green, pink, blue) over yellow. A comedy promoter whose logo is a playful pile of cards.
A big photo feature with its headline in white, a stack of small stories with city pill tags, then a row of destinations. A travel magazine with a clean newspaper rhythm.
